claim: For rooted full binary trees with unit-length edges, the variance \(V_T(k)\) of rooted phylogenetic diversity under uniform \(k\)-leaf rarefaction is unimodal for every tree with \(1\le n\le9\) leaves, and this cutoff is sharp: the 10-leaf tree whose root children are a perfect balanced 8-leaf subtree and a 2-leaf cherry has \(V_T(1),\ldots,V_T(10)=(16/25,136/225,28/45,1306/2205,1916/3969,3884/11025,2/9,8/81,0,0)\), with \(V_T(1)>V_T(2)<V_T(3)>V_T(4)\), so its variance curve is not unimodal.

correctness.rationale: The rooted-PD edge indicator representation gives the stated clade-covariance variance identity. Exact rational subset enumeration verifies the witness curve and strict inequalities; the exhaustive Catalan recursion checks every rooted plane full binary shape through nine leaves, which covers all rooted full binary shapes.

originality.rationale: The claim is not a restatement of the known general rarefaction variance formula: it establishes a sharp finite unimodality threshold and an explicit exact counterexample. Primary full text and actual published-finding corpus queries were checked; remaining novelty risk is recorded rather than treated as eliminated.
residual_risks: Search and ledger partitions cannot establish global uniqueness; an unindexed paper or result may contain an equivalent variance-shape counterexample.

The finite census does not bound the number or location of variance peaks for trees with more than ten leaves.

value.rationale: Variance under rarefaction is used to quantify sampling uncertainty in phylogenetic diversity. The sharp ten-leaf boundary gives a concrete warning against universal one-peak assumptions in variance-based sample-depth interpretation; the witness is small, natural, and exactly reproducible.
